Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 37, English)
Mantra vs. Tantra: What Actually Separates Them, and Why the Same Hanuman Mantra Can Be Either

Sour ce: a live, highly interactive Ashaeiynn sangat class (~56 minutes) built ar ound a single central question posed to the sangat — "what is the actual differ ence between mantra and tantra?" — with the sangat offering many competing guesses befor e Bhaiya lays out the teaching's actual answer: the sattvic/tamasic natur e of the mantra itself, not the object, deity , or appar ent intention involved.
1. The Central Question and the Sangat's Initial Guesses

1. Bhaiya opens by posing a direct question to the sangat: what is the real dif ference between mantra and tantra, given that tantra practice also uses mantras? Multiple sangat members of fer competing theories in real time: that tantra involves a special shape/angle (yantra) used alongside mantra; that yantra plus mantra together produce tantra; that intention (bhaav/intention) is what dif fers; that tantra specifically uses "things" (objects) for a particular purpose, often to cause harm; and that becoming a tantrik first requires "siddhi" through shamshan (cremation-ground) sadhna. 2. Bhaiya systematically rules out each of these popular guesses over the course of the session, using concrete counter - examples (detailed below), before revealing what this teaching considers the actual, precise distinction.
2. Why "Y antra + Mantra = Tantra" Doesn't Hold Up

1. Counter -example used to dismiss the yantra-based theory: many households keep a Lakshmi yantra or Shri yantra at home and read mantras in front of it as ordinary worship (e.g., Surya yantra, or a Hanuman Ji Maharaj yantra used for sadhna) — by the yantra+mantra theory , this common devotional practice would itself have to be classified as "tantra," which this teaching states is clearly not the case.
3. Why "Any Object-Based Ritual Action" Doesn't Define Tantra Either

1. Counter -example used to dismiss the object-based theory: a common folk practice of "warding of f" negativity by waving an object (a lemon, food, a piece of cloth) over a person and discarding it at a crossroads is popularly called "tantra." Bhaiya uses a live, playful example (waving a towel over sangat member "Ritesh" and discarding it) to interrogate this claim with the group — concluding that this action alone, without any specific mantra involved, doesn't automatically make it "tantra" either; a mantra or prayer must actually be present for the term to properly apply .
4. The Teaching's Actual Definition: Tantra Is a Mantra With a Tamasic Disposition

1. After systematically dismissing the yantra-based and object-based theories, Bhaiya offers this teaching's central definition: "T antra ka matlab woh mantra jiske andar tamsik pravritti hai" — tantra means specifically a mantra that carries a tamasic (dark/for ceful) disposition or energy . Mantra and tantra are not fundamentally two separate practices; tantra is best understood as a specific, tamasic-natur ed branch or category of mantra itself.

2. The deity invoked does not determine whether a mantra is "mantra" or "tantra" — the same deity (Hanuman Ji Maharaj, in the examples given) can be approached through either a sattvic mantra or a tamasic one; what dif fers is the underlying nature/disposition of the specific mantra used, not which deity is being addressed.
5. Sattvic vs. Tamasic Hanuman Mantras: Concr ete Examples

1. Sattvic example given: the short, simple "Om Hum Hanumate Namah" bija mantra, and "Shri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram" — described as extremely sattvic (Bhaiya notes his own preferred mantra is deliberately the smallest and simplest of all). 2. Tamasic example given: longer , elaborate bija-mantra strings such as "Om Hum Hanumate Ramdoot Mahabale Mahavir Hum Hum Hum Hreem Hum Hum Rom Rom Rom Hum Hum Phat Swaha" and its variants (e.g., ending in dif ferent bijas like "Reem," "Rom Rom Rom") — described as carrying tamasic disposition, and as the type of mantra commonly given out at well-known lar ge Hanuman institutions/"dhams" as a quick-fix solution to a visitor's stated problem, often prescribed with a specific repetition count (108 times, 1 1 rounds of mala, etc.). 3. The Panchmukhi Hanuman Ji Maharaj bija mantra "Rum" is given as a particularly potent tamasic example — Bhaiya states that chanting it continuously for even an hour can cause the practitioner's own body to tremble and produce fear , illustrating the forceful, tamasic character of this category of mantra directly and experientially .
6. Why Tamasic Mantras Work Faster , and What That Actually Means

1. A tamasic mantra activates ("siddh" hoti hai) comparatively quickly — at r oughly 1.25 lakh, 2.5 lakh, or 5 lakh repetitions — because, per this teaching, the deity is compelled/bound ("baadhit hokar") into acting rather than genuinely pleased ("prasann hokar") into acting. The practitioner is essentially working through a forceful "sound ef fect"- driven mechanism rather than through devotional pleasing. 2. By contrast, a sattvic mantra r equires vastly mor e repetition to activate — typically a minimum of one cr or e (10 million) jaaps — both the Panchakshar mantra "Om Namah Shivaya" and "Jai Siya Ram" are given as examples requiring this minimum threshold before full activation.
7. Why Every Tantrik Pr esents Himself as an Ordinary Devotee

1. A key observed pattern: no tantrik ever describes himself as a "tantrik." He will instead describe himself as a devotee of a specific deity — "I am a devotee of Hanuman Ji Maharaj," "I am a devotee of Bholenath," "I am a devotee of Mata Kali" — since, per this teaching's definition, it is the tamasic vs. sattvic nature of the specific mantra practiced (not the deity named or the practitioner's self-description) that actually determines whether the practice functions as tantra.
8. A Real Case: A Temple Priest Who Used Vashikaran, and What Happened

1. Bhaiya shar es a specific case involving two siblings who were af fected by a tantric af fliction traced back to a Hanuman devotee who sits in a temple, serves as its priest, and performs regular puja and sadhna there. This same devotee had previously used a tamasic mantra to attempt vashikaran (for ced contr ol) against a woman — the siblings' mother — attempting to compel Hanuman Ji Maharaj into making her fall for him through his jaap. 2. The attempt failed, since destiny (niyati) cannot be overridden this way — the woman never came under his control. However , the children the devotee later had with a differ ent woman wer e sick from birth — of fered as this teaching's account of the consequence carried by the perpetrator's own family line, even though he continued to appear outwardly devout, maintaining his position and temple service. 3. Bhaiya poses the r esulting question dir ectly to the sangat: who, in this case, should actually be called the "tantrik"? Both the temple priest and Bhaiya himself were, in this framing, chanting the exact same deity's (Hanuman Ji Maharaj's) mantra — the difference was that the priest's mantra was tamasic, while the sattvic mantra Bhaiya practices works only with the deity's genuine permission , not through compulsion.
9. Why "Jai Siya Ram" Is Consider ed Supreme Among Hanuman-Related Mantras

1. This teaching describes "Jai Siya Ram" as ranking above all other Hanuman Ji Maharaj mantras specifically because of its extreme subtlety (sookshmata) — it is described as so fine/subtle that it has no "kaat" (counter/cut) — meaning nothing can ef fectively counteract or neutralize it once fully activated. 2. Its activation thr eshold is corr espondingly high — r oughly 50 lakh to 1 cr or e repetitions — but once activated, this teaching states it is capable of cutting through even lar ge, powerful tantric workings directed against a practitioner .
10. Not Everything Needs to Be "Pur ely Sattvic" — All Three Gunas Have a Role

1. A nuance offer ed mid-session, illustrated by a live example: during an ongoing exorcism/cleansing occurring in real time for a sangat member af fected by tamasic-mantra-based af fliction, the doots (deity's messengers) actively working to remove the affliction must themselves adopt an "ugra" (fierce/forceful) disposition to do so ef fectively — this "ugra tattva" is itself tamasic in natur e, illustrating that all thr ee gunas (sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic) ar e described as necessary , valid forms of energy , not simply "good vs. bad." 2. This nuance dir ectly connects to why Bhagwan Shiv is called the master of tamasic energy — this is not, per this teaching, evidence against his capacity for moksha or divinity; all three ener gies are described as valid paths capable of leading toward moksha, when properly understood.
1 1. Tantra Pr ovides Energy , Not Moksha Dir ectly

1. In response to a live question about whether tantra (being tamasic) can still lead to moksha, Bhaiya clarifies: tantra itself does not grant moksha — tantra pr ovides energy (urja), and that energy can be used to obtain many things, but moksha is a separate matter entirely . 2. Bhaiya r eferences the institute's own prior "Mool Tatva" class/video as the corr ect place to pr operly understand what moksha actually is — cautioning that most people who ask for or expect moksha don't actually understand its true definition or what genuinely follows from attaining it.
12. A Personal, Practical Philosophy: Don't Simply Wait for Karma to Resolve Itself

1. Bhaiya states his own explicit philosophy: he does not r ecommend simply waiting for karmic consequence (karma-phal) to naturally catch up with someone who has wr onged you or your family — while af firming that the principle of karma is real, he notes it can take a very long time to manifest, "enough time for a whole life to pass." 2. His recommended alternative: build drishti (per ceptive insight) first, shakti (spiritual power) second, and maintain a guru's supportive hand third — and when someone deliberately tar gets you or your family through tantric means, respond decisively rather than passively waiting. 3. A personal example offer ed as a cautionary tale: a devotee who had performed consistent jaap for 30 straight years had that entire accumulated jaap "eaten" by an unaddressed negativity , because he refused to have it removed, insisting that "God will see to it" rather than taking direct action — illustrating the cost of pure passive faith without personal astral-world awareness or action.
13. Why Relying Entir ely on Others (Priests, Institutions) Without Personal Drishti Is Risky

1. A further caution: some temple priests and spiritually accomplished individuals may per ceive when a visiting devotee has independently built up genuine siddhi (thr ough their own long, hard-earned sadhna) — and may act to absorb or "wrap up" (lapet न ा) that siddhi for themselves , rather than the visitor themselves recognizing and protecting what they have built, since they lack the drishti to notice. 2. This is offer ed as a key practical r eason to build one's own drishti rather than depending entir ely on visits to temples or other practitioners — genuine protection and awareness of what's happening around a person (including around family members) requires personal astral-world literacy , not just outward devotion.
14. Personal Testimony: How Long Bhaiya's Own Drishti Took to Develop

1. Bhaiya shar es that gaining darshan (vision/contact) with his own guru took him a full year of dedicated effort , after which his guru revealed his specific kul devta (family deity) and the full extent of tantric af flictions af fecting him, instructing him that he himself would need to personally fight through and resolve each of them. 2. Bhaiya notes his guru could have r emoved all of it instantly with a single blessing but deliberately chose not to — instead guiding him step by step while requiring him to personally do the work — because, per this teaching, even far more advanced saints and mahatmas remain deeply engaged in their own ongoing sadhna, and personal ef fort is what this teaching values and models.
15. On Why Some Are Called Tantriks: A Closing Reframe

1. This teaching describes tantriks, in a br oad sense, as often being individuals whose ordinary worldly capabilities/intelligence wer en't sufficient to succeed thr ough conventional paths — but who nonetheless hold genuine astral-world knowledge that most people lack. The teaching's explicit encouragement is not to fear or dismiss this knowledge, but to personally learn it — since ordinary people are described as generally more capable than tantriks in most other respects, but simply uneducated in this specific domain.
16. The Body Runs on Mor e Than Food: A Supporting Observation

1. Bhaiya offers an observation in support of the astral world's r eality: some saints/mahatmas ar e described as surviving on water alone with no appar ent ill effect, while some people who car efully follow strict diet charts still develop chr onic health pr oblems — of fered as evidence that the physical body's functioning isn't fully explainable through food/diet alone, and that subtle-world (sookshma jagat) factors play a real, underappreciated role.
17. Family Discouragement of Long Practice, and a Pointed Observation

1. Bhaiya notes a common pattern: family members who discourage a person fr om spending long hours on jaap ("why ar e you sitting ther e chanting Ram Ram Ram for so long, go get educated and succeed instead") ar e often the very same people who quietly consult others (astr ologers, priests) befor e any major family decision, or when something goes wr ong at home — of fered as a pointed observation about the inconsistency of dismissing astral-world practice outright while still relying on it indirectly during a crisis.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Tantra is not a separate practice fr om mantra — it is a specific, tamasic-natur ed branch or category of mantra itself. The deity invoked, the objects used, or the practitioner's stated intention do not by themselves determine whether something is "tantra"; the deciding factor is whether the specific mantra used carries a tamasic (forceful/compelling) or sattvic (pleasing/devotional) disposition. Tamasic mantras activate quickly (r oughly 1.25-5 lakh r epetitions) because they compel/bind the deity into acting; sattvic mantras r equire far mor e repetition (a minimum of about one cr or e) because they work only through the deity's genuine pleasure and permission. No genuine tantrik calls himself a "tantrik" — he presents himself as an ordinary devotee of a specific deity; the mantra's nature, not the practitioner's self-description, is what actually determines the classification. "Jai Siya Ram" is consider ed supreme among Hanuman-r elated mantras due to its extreme subtlety — it has no ef fective counter once fully activated (roughly 50 lakh to 1 crore repetitions), though it takes considerable ef fort to reach that point. Sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic energies ar e all described as necessary and valid — even a devotional cleansing/exorcism can require a forceful ("ugra"/tamasic) disposition to be ef fective; this isn't automatically "bad." Tantra pr ovides energy (urja), not moksha dir ectly — moksha is a separate, deeper matter requiring its own proper understanding (see the institute's "Mool Tatva" teaching for the fuller framework).

Waiting passively for karma to r esolve wr ongdoing against you or your family is not this teaching's r ecommended appr oach — building your own drishti, shakti, and guru support, and responding decisively when genuinely wronged, is preferred over pure passive faith. Genuine siddhi built through personal, hard-earned sadhna can potentially be per ceived and absorbed by others who have their own developed drishti if the practitioner themselves lacks the awareness to protect it — a key reason to build personal astral-world literacy rather than relying entirely on outside practitioners or institutions. A guru may deliberately choose not to instantly r emove a disciple's afflictions , even when capable of doing so, in order to have the disciple personally engage in and learn from the process. Family members who discourage long spiritual practice ar e often the same people who quietly r ely on similar practices/consultations during a personal crisis — a pointed but not universal observation about inconsistency , not a blanket criticism of families. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 37, English)
Mantra vs. Tantra: What Actually Separates Them, and Why the Same Hanuman Mantra Can Be Either
User-style questions with answers gr ounded in this Ashaeiynn live sangat class. Gr eeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. What's the actual differ ence between mantra and tantra? A: Per this teaching, tantra is not a separate practice from mantra at all — it is specifically a mantra that carries a tamasic (dark/forceful) disposition. Mantra and tantra aren't two dif ferent things; tantra is best understood as a tamasic-natured branch or category within mantra itself.

Q2. Does combining a yantra (sacr ed diagram) with a mantra turn it into tantra? A: No — this teaching explicitly rejects this idea. Many households keep a Lakshmi yantra or Shri yantra and read mantras in front of it as completely ordinary devotional worship; by this logic that common practice would have to count as "tantra," which this teaching states is clearly not the case.

Q3. Is any object-based ritual (like waving a lemon or food over someone and discarding it) automatically "tantra"? A: Not by itself — per this teaching, the action alone, without an actual mantra or prayer involved, doesn't make something tantra. A mantra must actually be present for the term to properly apply; the object-based action alone is not the deciding factor .

Q4. Does the specific deity being worshipped determine whether a practice is mantra or tantra? A: No — per this teaching, the same deity (Hanuman Ji Maharaj, in the examples given) can be approached through either a sattvic or a tamasic mantra. What dif fers is the disposition of the specific mantra used, not which deity is being addressed.

Q5. Can you give an example of a sattvic vs. a tamasic Hanuman mantra? A: Per this teaching, "Om Hum Hanumate Namah" and "Shri Ram Jai Ram Jai Jai Ram" are given as sattvic examples — short and simple. Longer , elaborate bija-mantra strings (e.g., "Om Hum Hanumate Ramdoot Mahabale Mahavir Hum Hum Hum..." and its variants) are given as tamasic examples, often prescribed at well-known lar ge institutions as a quick-fix solution.

Q6. Why do tamasic mantras seem to work faster than sattvic ones? A: Per this teaching, a tamasic mantra activates at a comparatively low repetition threshold (roughly 1.25-5 lakh) because it compels or binds the deity into acting rather than genuinely pleasing them into it. A sattvic mantra requires vastly more repetition (a minimum of about one crore) because it works only through the deity's genuine pleasure and permission.

Q7. Does chanting the Panchmukhi Hanuman bija mantra "Rum" have any noticeable physical effect? A: Per this teaching, yes — chanting it continuously for even an hour is described as potentially causing the practitioner's own body to tremble and produce fear , illustrating the forceful, tamasic character of this category of mantra directly and experientially .

Q8. Would a r eal tantrik ever describe himself as a "tantrik"? A: No — per this teaching, no genuine tantrik presents himself this way . He will instead describe himself as an ordinary devotee of a specific deity (Hanuman Ji Maharaj, Bholenath, Mata Kali). It is the tamasic vs. sattvic nature of the specific mantra practiced, not the practitioner's self-description, that determines the classification.

Q9. What happened in the case of the temple priest who tried vashikaran on someone's mother? A: Per this teaching's account, a devotee who served as a temple priest attempted vashikaran (forced control) against a woman using a tamasic Hanuman mantra, trying to compel the deity into making her fall for him. The attempt failed because destiny (niyati) cannot be overridden this way , but the children he later had with a dif ferent woman were sick from birth — described as the consequence carried by his own family line, even as he continued outwardly appearing devout.

Q10. In that case, who should actually be called the "tantrik" — the priest or an ordinary devotee chanting the same deity's name? A: Per this teaching, both may be chanting the exact same deity's mantra, but the priest's mantra was tamasic (used to compel), while a sattvic mantra works only with the deity's genuine permission. The distinguishing factor is the mantra's disposition, not surfacelevel devotion or temple af filiation.

Q1 1. Why is "Jai Siya Ram" consider ed especially powerful among Hanuman-r elated mantras? A: Per this teaching, its extreme subtlety (sookshmata) means it has no ef fective "kaat" (counter) — nothing can neutralize it once fully activated. Its activation threshold is high (roughly 50 lakh to 1 crore repetitions), but once activated it is described as capable of cutting through even lar ge, powerful tantric workings.

Q12. If tantra is tamasic, does that mean it's entir ely bad or that moksha is impossible thr ough it? A: Not necessarily "bad" — per this teaching, all three gunas (sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic) are described as necessary , valid forms of ener gy . Even a cleansing/exorcism in progress may require a forceful, "ugra" (tamasic) disposition from the deity's messengers to be ef fective. This is also why Bhagwan Shiv is called the master of tamasic ener gy without that implying he lacks capacity for moksha.

Q13. Does tantra itself grant moksha? A: No — per this teaching, tantra provides ener gy (urja), which can be used to obtain many things, but moksha is a separate, deeper matter . This teaching points to the institute's "Mool Tatva" class for a fuller understanding of what moksha actually means.

Q14. If someone deliberately wr ongs me or my family , should I just wait for karma to catch up with them? A: Per this teaching's stated philosophy , this isn't the recommended approach — while karma is real, it can take a very long time to manifest ("enough for a whole life to pass"). The recommended alternative is to build your own drishti, shakti, and guru support, and respond decisively rather than waiting passively .

Q15. What happened to the devotee who did 30 years of consistent jaap but r efused to r emove an attached negativity? A: Per this teaching's account, that entire 30 years of accumulated jaap was "eaten" by the unaddressed negativity , because the devotee insisted "God will see to it" rather than taking direct action to remove it — of fered as a cautionary example of the cost of pure passive faith without personal astral-world awareness.

Q16. Is it risky to r ely entir ely on temple priests or outside practitioners instead of developing my own spiritual awar eness? A: Yes, per this teaching — some practitioners with developed drishti may perceive when a visitor has independently built up genuine siddhi through their own hard-earned sadhna, and may act to absorb it, since the visitor themselves lacks the awareness to notice or protect what they've built.

Q17. How long did it take Bhaiya himself to develop his own drishti? A: Per this teaching, gaining darshan (contact) with his own guru took a full year of dedicated ef fort; his guru then revealed his kul devta and the tantric af flictions af fecting him, instructing him to personally fight through and resolve each one, rather than removing them instantly .

Q18. Why would a guru choose not to instantly r emove a disciple's afflictions if he's capable of doing so? A: Per this teaching, this is deliberate — requiring the disciple to personally engage in and learn from the process, consistent with the observation that even far more advanced saints remain deeply engaged in their own ongoing sadhna rather than having everything handed to them.

Q19. Are tantriks generally mor e knowledgeable or capable than ordinary people? A: Per this teaching, tantriks are often described as people whose ordinary worldly capabilities weren't suf ficient for conventional success, but who hold genuine astral-world

knowledge that most people lack — the teaching's explicit encouragement is to personally learn this knowledge rather than fear or dismiss it, since ordinary people are generally more capable in most other respects.

Q20. Does the human body run pur ely on food and diet? A: Not entirely , per this teaching — some saints/mahatmas are described as surviving on water alone with no apparent ill ef fect, while some people who carefully follow strict diet charts still develop chronic health problems, of fered as evidence that subtle-world (sookshma jagat) factors play a real, underappreciated role in how the body actually functions.

Q21. My family discourages me fr om spending long hours on jaap — how does this teaching frame that? A: This teaching points out a pattern (not a universal rule): family members who discourage long practice are often the same people who quietly consult astrologers or priests before major decisions or during a crisis — an observed inconsistency in dismissing astral-world practice outright while still relying on it indirectly .
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 37 additions)

Always frame the mantra-vs-tantra distinction as this teaching's own specific definition (tamasic disposition of the mantra itself) — never suggest yantra use, ritual objects, or the deity invoked alone determine the classification, since this teaching explicitly walks through and rejects those alternative theories. When discussing sattvic vs. tamasic mantras, keep the framing neutral about the deity involved — the same deity (e.g., Hanuman Ji Maharaj) can be approached through either kind of mantra; never imply one deity is inherently "tantric" and another inherently "safe." Present the vashikaran/temple-priest case study as this teaching's own illustrative account, not as a claim being independently verified — and preserve the point that the mantra's nature, not outward devotion or a temple position, determined the classification. Keep the "tantra provides ener gy , not moksha" distinction intact — never conflate tantric practice with attaining moksha when answering questions grounded in this teaching. When discussing the "don't just wait for karma" philosophy , present it as this teaching's own recommended approach (build drishti/shakti/guru support, respond decisively) rather than a universal ethical prescription — and never frame the recommended response as literal real-world confrontation or vigilantism. Preserve the caution about relying entirely on outside practitioners without personal drishti — frame this as encouragement toward personal spiritual literacy , not distrust of teachers in general. When discussing family discouragement of practice, keep the tone observational rather than accusatory — present it as a pattern this teaching notices, not a blanket criticism of all families. Part III — Curated Conversational Q&A (Hinglish)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Curated Conversational Supplement (Session 37, Hinglish)
Mantra aur Tantra ke Fark par Sangat ki Live Guessing Game aur Baatcheet

Yeh Part III har session mein nahi hota — sirf tab jab sour ce transcript mein genuine live sangat conversation ho. Y eh session almost poora hi ek live, interactive Socratic discussion ke format mein hai — sangat members ne mantra-tantra ke fark ke baar e mein kaafi guesses diye, ek member (Abhishek bhai) ne apna specific theory rakha, aur ek member ne apni aura-checking testimony shar e ki. Yeh EXHAUSTIVE transcript nahi hai — is poori lively discussion mein se sirf sabse valuable aur repr esentative exchanges chune gaye hain. Har exchange ke baad ek italicized note hai jo bataata hai yeh kyun include kiya gaya.
Bhaiya (opening question): आज मुझे मैं जानना चाहता हूं िक मंत्र और तंत्र में फक� क्या है?

Sangat members (multiple, live guesses): यंत्र और मंत्र जब िमल जाए तो तंत्र बन जाता... भाव अलग होते हैं ना, इंटेंशन भी... तंत्र में कोई चीज िकसी चीज का पिट�कुलर यूज़ करते हैं, हािन पहुंचाने के िलए यूज़ िकया जाए वो तंत्र है शायद ... िसद्ध होना चािहए पहले , अच्छा तांित्रक िसद्ध होना चािहए पहले।

Bhaiya: अच्छा चलो बहुत लोग यह बोलते हैं... लक्ष्मी यंत्र घर में रखते हैं, उसके आगे मंत्र पढ़ो तो वो तंत्र बन जाएगा — इनके िहसाब से लक्ष्मी यंत्र जो घर में रखते हैं वह तंत्र हो गया। ऑिब्वयसली तो वो बात हम बोल नहीं सकते।

Yeh opening exchange isliye include kiya gaya kyunki yeh poori session ka tone set karta hai — ek live "guessing game" jisme sangat active participants hain, na ki sirf passive listeners. Bhaiya ka har guess ko r espectfully consider karke systematically r eject karna teaching style ki ek achi misaal hai.
Bhaiya (Ritesh ke स ाथ live demonstration): मान लो मैंने यह जो टॉवल है यह िरतेश के ऊपर से वार के मैंने चौराहे पर छोड़ िदया, बताओ तंत्र हो गया?
Sangat member: भैया है तो तंत्र का पाट� है।
